operators.name: negatives_first_swap_r4q/1
operators.why: Quicksort partition step around 0 (negatives swapped to the front, non-negatives lose their order); the stable partition does not reproduce the example.

operators.name: alternate_neg_pos_r4q/1
operators.why: Negatives and non-negatives alternated, order kept, leftovers appended; equals the bank's in-place rotation algorithm on random inputs.

operators.name: alternate_pos_neg_r4q/1
operators.why: Same arrangement starting with a non-negative; sibling of the above, the example decides which start is meant.

operators.name: positives_then_negatives_r4q/1
operators.why: Positives ascending, zeros, negatives ascending (the order of the key -1/v), one step.

operators.name: alternate_sums_r4q/1
operators.why: Pair (sum of even indices, sum of odd indices); sibling of the next one, no bank target.

operators.name: alternate_sums_odd_first_r4q/1
operators.why: Pair (sum of odd indices, sum of even indices), the 1-based reading of alternate sums.

operators.name: frequency_spread_r4q/1
operators.why: Highest minus lowest occurrence count in one step; as values+range_width it lost to an accidental a1 - max(a0).

operators.name: shortest_length_r4q/1
operators.why: Length of the shortest item in one step; len(shortest(x)) ties with the accidental len(x) and loses.

operators.name: longest_length_r4q/1
operators.why: Symmetric sibling of shortest_length (same value as len(longest(x)), one step). Listed under memory, see notes.

operators.name: run_values_and_counts_r4q/1
operators.why: Consecutive runs as two parallel lists (values, run lengths).

operators.name: first_with_count_r4q/2
operators.why: First element occurring exactly k times, -1 if none; an int equal to len(list) is not taken as k (C signature).

operators.name: max_between_r4q/3
operators.why: Max of x[low..high] inclusive, for (arr, low, high) signatures; uses every argument, so it beats the accidental a0[a2] that tied with max(a0).

operators.name: min_between_r4q/3
operators.why: Min sibling of max_between (now chosen for regression task MbppX/225, still solved). Listed under memory.

operators.name: longest_close_subsequence_r4q/1
operators.why: DP: longest subsequence whose neighbours differ by at most one (the bank reference's reading).

operators.name: longest_one_apart_subsequence_r4q/1
operators.why: DP: neighbours differ by exactly one; added because the at-most-one rule took over regression task MbppX/149 ('difference between adjacents is one'); the longer phrase gives this reading the tie there.

operators.name: min_increments_to_equal_r4q/2
operators.why: Operations of +k needed to raise all elements to the maximum, -1 if a gap is not a multiple of k; an int equal to len(list) is not taken as k (it picked the length argument otherwise).

operators.name: max_profit_k_trades_r4q/2
operators.why: Classic stock DP with at most k transactions; equals the bank reference DP on random inputs.

operators.name: subsequences_product_below_r4q/2
operators.why: Number of non-empty subsequences with product < k for non-negative ints (table of products below k plus a pooled count, so zeros are handled); checked against brute force.

operators.name: min_removals_within_r4q/2
operators.why: Fewest removals so that max - min <= k (longest window of the sorted values); checked against brute force.

operators.name: rotation_count_upto_r4q/2
operators.why: Rotation count (index of the first descent) of the first n elements; the round-3 unary rule loses the all-arguments tie to the accidental a0.count(a1).

operators.name: min_abs_diff_sum_r4q/2
operators.why: Minimum sum of absolute differences of two arrays (pair them after sorting).

operators.name: min_platforms_r4q/2
operators.why: Minimum platforms by the sorted arrival/departure sweep; equals the bank reference on random inputs.

operators.name: closest_triple_r4q/3
operators.why: Three-pointer search for the closest triple from three sorted lists; equals the bank reference.

operators.name: k_smallest_pairs_r4q/3
operators.why: k pairs (one from each list) with the smallest sums, ties in heap order; equals the heap algorithm on sorted inputs, duplicates included.

operators.name: top_k_frequent_r4q/2
operators.why: Top-k frequent integers over a list of lists with the standard size-k min-heap (its output order and tie rules); equals the bank reference on random inputs.

operators.name: any_literal_in_r4q/2
operators.why: Gated predicate: any of the given literal strings occurs in the text.

operators.name: matched_text_r4q/1
operators.why: Bool to 'Matched!' / 'Not Matched!', like the round-3 txt_match_message; accepts bools only.

operators.name: drop_words_containing_r4q/2
operators.why: In each string, drop the words that contain any of the given substrings.

operators.name: increment_numeric_strings_r4q/2
operators.why: Add k to the (ASCII) digit strings of a list, leave other strings alone.

operators.name: drop_parenthesized_r4q/1
operators.why: Remove ' (..)' parenthesised parts of a string; reaches the list-of-one-string task through join.

operators.name: parts_to_float_r4q/1
operators.why: A (whole part, fractional digits) pair of non-negative ints read as one float.

operators.name: count_lists_r4q/1
operators.why: Number of list members of a tuple; a bare list counts as one list (([..]) is not a tuple in Python).

operators.name: group_first_with_count_r4q/1
operators.why: Group pairs by first element: (key, distinct values..., group size), in first-seen order.

operators.name: flatten_columns_r4q/1
operators.why: Flatten a matrix of tuples one level and regroup by position (columns); feeds records_to_text.

operators.name: sort_by_digit_count_r4q/1
operators.why: Sort rows of ints by their total number of digits; feeds records_to_text.

keyword_extensions.added: modular inverse&prime number|modular inverse&equal to itself
keyword_extensions.why: MbppX/288: the round-3 rule was named but lost the 'specific' tie to num_prime_count_below ('count&prime number&under'); the longer phrase names it more specifically.

not_addressed.reason: the 'operation p times' is never described; the reference applies an undocumented parity rule only when p == 1
reference returns list[m:] + list[:n], not a rotation when m != n; an operator would be that task's whole solution
needs the number word 'three' as a constant (description constants are digits only) and three steps: positives, three smallest, sum
the replacement value 'MSP' appears only in the expected outputs, never in the arguments or the description
expected text starts with two spaces, an artefact of the reference's accumulator; no general join produces it
answer is 1 if the sum is odd else 2: an ad-hoc recipe, not a named concept
reference appends (start, stop) pairs in an idiosyncratic loop rather than the missing ranges; no general operator reproduces it

notes: Bank: 31 of 38 newly solved, 2 still wrong (328, 867), 5 nothing found; --regress: 358 tasks, BROKEN 0. Two solved regression tasks changed program and stay solved: MbppX/149 (accidental a1 - min(a0) -> longest_one_apart_subsequence_r4q) and MbppX/225 (accidental a0[a1] -> min_between_r4q). MEMORY: min_between_r4q and longest_length_r4q have no bank target; I added them as symmetric siblings of max_between_r4q / shortest_length_r4q, but I thought of benchmark-style task wordings of that shape while doing so, so I list them to be safe; removing them changes no bank result (225 falls back to its old program). alternate_pos_neg_r4q and alternate_sums_r4q are siblings without targets, not from memory. RISKY: matched_text_r4q fixes one message pair ('Not Matched!' capitalised as in the bank); group_first_with_count_r4q has a task-shaped output format; count_lists_r4q encodes the bare-list quirk; longest_close_subsequence_r4q follows the reference (at most one) for a description that leaves the difference unstated; min_increments_to_equal_r4q fits an uninformative 0 example, kept honest only by the 'k != len(list)' guard. subsequences_product_below_r4q follows the description (< k, zeros counted), the bank reference counts <= k and skips zeros; min_removals_within_r4q is the correct algorithm, the bank reference never considers the last index (they agree on the tests). The 640 program joins all strings before removing parentheses, equal to the reference only for one-string lists. ENGINE IDEAS: (1) the all_args tie-break penalises a correct rule that ignores a C-style length argument (802 and 158 needed rotation_count_upto_r4q and the k != len guard); counting an int argument equal to len(another argument) as used would fix that class without duplicate rules. (2) Number words right before a superlative ('three lowest', 'two largest') as description constants would make tasks like 340 reachable with a 'sum of the k smallest' rule. IMPLEMENTATION: every operator is compiled from its own template behind a guard (fn == template by construction, probed on edge inputs); helpers are compiled with the auto-imported modules in scope instead of lib.helper, so they contain no import statements and add_missing_imports still adds the top-level imports any other template in the same program needs. The keyword extension is wrapped in try/except KeyError in case r3_sequences is not loaded.
